correctness.rationale: The linear-first Gram recursion gives the coefficient convolution M_1 F_f=M_f with the conjugated atom coordinates. Clearing denominators gives Q=(1-a)+a(z-1)^2, a=(1+2 cos ε)/3. Both simple poles are outside the closed unit disk throughout the claimed interval. Evaluating the residues using h=z−1=±iε/√3+O(ε³) gives leading numerator coefficients (2/3, −1/3∓1/√3, −1/3±1/√3) times ε²/3. The two rows are orthogonal with Euclidean squared norm 4/3. In the stated weighted domain norm the leading residue map has norm ε/√3, with an operator-norm error O(ε²). The reciprocal poles have modulus r=1−ε²/6+O(ε⁴) and phases ±θ with θ=ε/√3+O(ε³). In the squared geometric-weight mean the relative cross term is bounded by (1−r)/|1−r exp(2iθ)|=O(ε). Cauchy–Schwarz then gives the uniform upper bound; a unit input parallel to either leading residue row kills the other row at leading order and attains the bound by the reverse triangle inequality. Multiplication by r/(1−r) gives 2√3 after scaling by ε; the zeroth coefficient is bounded independently of ε. For fixed separation the absolutely convergent series evaluates to f at each atom, since the common simple singularity of M_f and M_1 has ratio f at that atom. This verifies both the optimum constant and absolute reconstruction.
residual_risks: The proof is for the specified three equal masses, order, norm and coefficient functional; it gives no exact finite-separation optimizer or observations-to-reconstruction noise bound.

value.rationale: Finite-support absolute convergence is qualitative and does not distinguish well-separated from nearly coincident samples. This minimal symmetric example beyond the planar case quantifies precisely the loss of uniformity and separates the effects of pole damping, oscillatory cancellation and residue geometry. The constant is a benchmark for coefficient estimates, not just another demonstration of convergence.
residual_risks: The benchmark is narrow and does not establish sample-noise amplification or a general collision classification.
